name: Tali (Tali Mahadeva) Temple
tagline: Historic city Shiva temple at the heart of Kozhikode's heritage circuit
summary: Tali Mahadeva Temple is a 14th‑century Shiva temple in central Kozhikode, tied to the Zamorin era and the Revathi Pattathanam scholarly tradition; it remains a living heritage site with morning and…
description: Tali Mahadeva Temple (commonly called Tali Temple) stands in the Palayam/Chalappuram quarter of Kozhikode and represents traditional Kerala temple architecture and the city's medieval civic-religious core.

The temple is closely associated with the Zamorin rulers and with the Revathi Pattathanam — an annual scholarly assembly historically held at the Tali — so it matters both as a place of worship and as a civic cultural landmark.

Visitors find a compact, atmospheric precinct: timber-roofed buildings, a temple tank (tali), lamp-lit evening rituals and small subsidiary shrines around the courtyard. The site regularly features in local heritage walks and responsible-tourism trails that finish at the Tali.

The temple functions as a living site: daily pujas, seasonal festivals and local ceremonies continue to draw devotees and visitors. Confirm specific puja times, special events and photography rules before you travel.
highlights: 14th‑century city Shiva temple tied to the Zamorin court
Revathi Pattathanam scholarly tradition connected to the precinct
Kerala-style timber and tiled temple architecture and tank (tali)
Atmospheric evening deepa-aradhana (lamp ritual) — a good visitor moment
Located inside Kozhikode city — easy to include on a heritage walk

sections.heading: Background
body: Tali Temple is one of Kozhikode’s oldest and most revered shrines and sits in the historic Palayam/Chalappuram area. Accounts and tourism sources place its origins in the medieval period and link the temple to the Zamorins’ patronage and to the city’s learned traditions.
The temple precinct historically hosted the Revathi Pattathanam, the famous scholarly assembly; that tradition continues in varying forms and contributes to the site's cultural importance.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Take in the main sanctum (Shiva lingam), the traditional Kerala timber-and-tile roofscape, the temple tank (the 'tali') and the subsidiary shrines that form the compact courtyard. The carved timber work, lamp-pillars and courtyard layout show the local temple-building idiom.

Time your visit for early morning puja or the evening deeparadhana (lamp ritual) for atmosphere — many visitors prefer dusk when the lamp-lighting and rituals make the precinct especially photogenic and devotional in character. Respect any photography restrictions, particularly inside the sanctum.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: The temple sits inside the city and is easy to add to a Kozhikode heritage circuit that includes nearby markets and colonial-era streets. Typical visitor flows peak in the cooler months (October–March) and during festival periods — check local listings for Revathi Pattathanam and Maha Shivaratri dates.

Daily routines commonly include morning and evening darshan windows; several visitor guides and the temple information pages list an evening reopening for darshan (confirm exact times with the temple). Dress modestly and follow local temple etiquette — remove footwear, avoid revealing clothing and follow staff guidance.

latest.text: Kerala Tourism lists Tali Temple on the Kozhikode life‑experience trail and highlights the site for heritage visitors; the page notes the temple’s architecture and its role in city trails.

Local temple listings and pilgrimage sites show the temple open for evening darshan (typical evening reopening around 17:00–20:30), making dusk visits and deepa-aradhana convenient for arriving tourists; confirm timings before you go.

visitorInfo.bestTime: October–March (cool, dry); dawn or dusk for the best atmosphere
visitorInfo.howToReach: In central Kozhikode (Palayam/Chalappuram). About 1 km from Kozhikode Railway Station — walk or take an auto/taxi. The temple is easy to include on a city heritage walk.
etiquette: Confirm current puja/darshan timings with the temple or local tourism office before you travel.
Respect dress and footwear rules; carry a shawl or scarf if you plan to enter the sanctum area.
Visit at dusk for deepa-aradhana (lamp ritual) but avoid crowded festival days unless you want the full experience.
Photography may be restricted inside the sanctum — ask permission and follow staff directions.
